# Entuned

> Entuned is a retail music strategy platform that turns customer psychology into store soundtracks — driving measurable sales lift. Not licensed catalog. Not a playlist service. Self-serve, starts free.

Entuned makes original music for retail stores. An owner-operator signs up free at app.entuned.co/start, picks an outcome (more dwell, more energy, bigger baskets), and the music plays in-browser the same day — no hardware, no contract, no card. Because the music is original and carries no PRO obligation, it removes the ASCAP/BMI/SESAC/GMR licensing question entirely. Paid tiers (Boost, $99/location/month; Professional, $399/location/month) tailor the music to the store's ideal customer profile and tie it to sales outcomes.

The category we operate in sits between the traditional in-store music business (Mood Media, Soundtrack Your Brand, SiriusXM Business, Cloud Cover) and the retail analytics business (RetailNext, Sensormatic, Standard AI). Those two categories have never shared data. That gap is where audio fails to show up as a measured variable in retail performance.

## Research Foundation

Four decades of peer-reviewed research on music and consumer behavior sit behind the category. Milliman (1982) established that tempo changes shopper pace and spending. Areni and Kim (1993) showed classical music in a wine shop moved customers toward more expensive bottles. Yalch and Spangenberg (2000) documented that familiar music shortens visits. These findings have been replicated across retail formats and decades.

## Blog Posts
- [What One Chord Does](https://entuned.co/blog/what-one-chord-does.html): A founder essay on why musicology could never hold a single fixed song still and move one internal parameter, and why generative models finally make that experiment cheap and repeatable.
- [Chill, Steady, Upbeat, All: What Each Free Mode Is For](https://entuned.co/blog/free-modes.html): Entuned Free gives your floor three mood modes, Chill, Steady, and Upbeat, plus an All setting that mixes them. What each is for, and what changes at Boost.
- [What in the Music Actually Moves the Sale](https://entuned.co/blog/what-in-the-music-moves-the-sale.html): Founder essay ranking the components of music by their effect on buying behavior: tempo entrainment, mode over key, the untested lyric lever, the familiarity paradox, volume, and song structure, each held against the field research.
- [Every Music Vendor Now Claims Music Boosts Sales. We Audited the Claims.](https://entuned.co/blog/music-vendor-claims-audit.html): A July 2026 audit of nine in-store music vendors' behavioral claims — what each claims, what substantiates it, and why none will measure the effect in a customer's own stores.
- [Is It Actually Illegal to Use Spotify in My Store?](https://entuned.co/blog/can-you-play-spotify-in-your-store.html): A clean answer for retail operators who just want to know if the Spotify account their store manager set up is going to bite them.
- [What Makes a Retail Music Strategy Effective? 5 Research-Backed Pillars](https://entuned.co/blog/what-makes-a-retail-music-strategy-effective-5-research-backed-pillars.html): An effective retail music strategy rests on five pillars: emotional targeting (especially in the first 5 minutes), sensory congruence across all channels, dynamic responsiveness to real-time condition
- [Can Music Be Optimized for Sales? Yes — Here's How](https://entuned.co/blog/can-music-be-optimized-for-sales-yes-heres-how.html): Yes, music can be optimized for sales the same way you'd optimize a landing page — by controlling individual variables and testing systematically.
- [What's the Best Retail Music Service? A Research-Based Evaluation](https://entuned.co/blog/whats-the-best-retail-music-service-a-research-based-evaluation.html): The best retail music service is the one that meets five research-backed criteria: real-time adaptability, parametric precision, brand congruence, familiarity avoidance, and measurement capability.
- [How Much Should Retailers Spend on Music? The ROI Math](https://entuned.co/blog/how-much-should-retailers-spend-on-music-the-roi-math.html): Retail music services cost $15-100/month per location, but the real question is ROI, not cost.
- [How Do You Measure the Impact of Music in Retail?](https://entuned.co/blog/how-do-you-measure-the-impact-of-music-in-retail.html): Measuring music's retail impact requires tracking three links: environment to emotion, emotion to behavior, behavior to purchase.
- [How Do You Choose Music for a Store? A Research-Backed Framework](https://entuned.co/blog/how-do-you-choose-music-for-a-store-a-research-backed-framework.html): Choosing music for a store requires starting with customer preference — not brand identity.
- [What to Do About an ASCAP or BMI Demand Letter](https://entuned.co/blog/ascap-bmi-demand-letter-what-to-do.html): A demand letter is a licensing demand, not a lawsuit. The real statutory range ($750 to $30,000 per work, willful up to $150,000), the 17 U.S.C. 110(5)(B) radio exemption, what to do the week the letter arrives, and three honest ways to resolve it.
- [Your Store Music Has a Second Audience: Your Staff](https://entuned.co/blog/what-store-music-does-to-your-staff.html): In-store music affects employees, not just customers — it lifts mood and routine-task work but impairs focused verbal work (Lesiuk 2005; Salamé & Baddeley 1989), and letting staff pick raises their satisfaction (Sanseverino 2022) while cutting customer sales ~6% (Daunfeldt 2021). The fix is a curated, intentional program both audiences can live with.
- [What Should Retailers Look for in a Music Provider?](https://entuned.co/blog/what-should-retailers-look-for-in-a-music-provider.html): Retailers should evaluate music providers on six research-backed criteria: real-time adaptability, parametric control, brand congruence, measurement capability, licensing clarity, and customer prefere
- [What Music Should a Supermarket Play? When It's Crowded, Speed Up](https://entuned.co/blog/what-music-should-a-supermarket-play.html): The slow-music rule (Milliman 1982) flips under crowding — a study of 43,676 baskets found fast-tempo music raised spending specifically when the store was crowded, by buying more items not pricier ones (Knoeferle et al. 2017). Tempo's real job in a grocery is regulating the energy of the crowd.
- [What Music Should a Restaurant Play? It Changes How the Food Tastes](https://entuned.co/blog/what-music-should-a-restaurant-play.html): Sound is closer to an ingredient than a backdrop — sonic seasoning shifts perceived taste (Crisinel & Spence 2012), volume steers diners toward healthy vs indulgent choices (Biswas et al. 2019), and slow tempo lengthens the meal and pours more drinks (Milliman 1986) — the bar lever a café has no bar to use.
- [What Music Should a Jewelry Store Play? What the Research Suggests](https://entuned.co/blog/what-music-should-a-jewelry-store-play.html): No jewelry-store study exists; the closest analog (Areni & Kim 1993, a wine store) found upscale music moved customers toward pricier items without changing dwell or quantity — it sets the price register, marked honestly as an inference.
- [What Music Should a Hotel Lobby Play? It's the Brand's First Sentence](https://entuned.co/blog/what-music-should-a-hotel-lobby-play.html): The lobby is the brand's first sentence — servicescape theory names music as shaping perception (Bitner 1992), classical music reads as more sophisticated (Wilson 2003), and music makes a wait feel better, not shorter (Hui, Dubé & Chébat 1997).
- [What Music Should a Flower Shop Play? There's Actually a Study](https://entuned.co/blog/what-music-should-a-flower-shop-play.html): A field experiment in an actual florist (Jacob et al. 2009) found romantic music lifted spending while the shop's usual pop music did no better than silence — the lever is musical fit, not just having music on.
- [What Music Should a Clothing Store Play? Why Letting Staff Pick Cost One Brand 11%](https://entuned.co/blog/what-music-should-a-clothing-store-play.html): A field experiment found letting staff control the music cut sales ~6% (~11% in womenswear) because whim-driven, high-energy tracks replaced a consistent baseline (Daunfeldt et al. 2021); music is a brand-identity signal to first-time shoppers (Beverland 2006), so the lever is curation discipline, not a tempo trick.
- [What Music Should a Bookshop Play? The Research Is Counterintuitive](https://entuned.co/blog/what-music-should-a-bookshop-play.html): Counterintuitive — familiar music shortens actual browsing while feeling longer; unfamiliar music stretches it while feeling shorter (Yalch & Spangenberg 2000); and music can shift selection without changing dwell at all (Areni & Kim 1993), so you have to choose the outcome.
- [What Music Should a Bar Play? Why the Volume Matters More Than the Song](https://entuned.co/blog/what-music-should-a-bar-play.html): A field experiment found raising bar music from ~72 to ~88 dB led beer drinkers to order more and drink faster (Guéguen et al. 2008) — the volume, not the song, drives the room's arousal and pace. Framed responsibly as a lever for setting a bar's energy by the hour, not maximizing consumption.
- [The Science of Store Music: How Sound Quietly Changes What People Buy](https://entuned.co/blog/the-science-of-store-music.html): The honest synthesis — a meta-analysis of 32 studies finds store-music effects are real but small and fit-dependent (Garlin & Owen 2006); the French/German wine study shows music can shift choice without shoppers noticing. The hub for the vertical-specific posts below.
- [How Do Retail Music Services Actually Work?](https://entuned.co/blog/how-do-retail-music-services-actually-work.html): Retail music services range from basic licensed playlists to adaptive, generative platforms that adjust in real time.
- [Calming Music for a Dog Grooming Salon: What the Research Actually Says](https://entuned.co/blog/calming-music-for-dog-grooming-salons.html): Wells 2002 and Bowman 2015 show the right music lowers canine stress, but dogs habituate to a looped track by the second day — so variety, not a static loop, is what keeps a grooming salon calm.
- [What Music Tempo Should a Coffee Shop Play? The Honest Answer](https://entuned.co/blog/best-music-tempo-for-a-coffee-shop.html): Slow tempo slows customer pace (Milliman 1982), but the famous restaurant spend lift came from alcohol over a longer sit — a café has no bar, so the lever is turnover-vs-lingering, and music people actually like (Caldwell & Hibbert 2002).
- [What's the Best BPM for Workout Music? What the Research Actually Says](https://entuned.co/blog/best-bpm-for-workout-music.html): The useful exercise tempo band is ~125-140 BPM with a ceiling around 140 (Karageorghis); music cuts perceived effort ~10% only at low-to-moderate intensity (Szmedra & Bacharach 1998); synchronizing to the beat, not the hype, drives most of the gain.
- [Why Some Stores Accidentally Push Customers Out the Door](https://entuned.co/blog/why-some-stores-accidentally-push-customers-out-the-door.html): Stores push customers away with well-intentioned sensory choices they think are improving the experience.
- [Why Playlist-Based Music Systems Consistently Underperform](https://entuned.co/blog/why-playlist-based-music-systems-consistently-underperform.html): Professionally curated playlists showed no significant sales effect across a 140-store field study — the largest retail music experiment ever conducted.
- [Store Music Licensing: The Operator's Guide to Playing Music Legally](https://entuned.co/blog/store-music-licensing.html): Why a personal Spotify account isn't legal in a store, what the four PROs charge, the narrow broadcast exemption, and the simplest compliant path.
- [Retail Sound Science: How Store Music Drives Shopper Behavior](https://entuned.co/blog/retail-sound-science.html): The research on how tempo, volume, familiarity, and musical fit move dwell time, willingness to pay, and perceived wait — with links to each lever in depth.
- [Retail Conversion and AOV: The Levers That Actually Move Them](https://entuned.co/blog/retail-conversion-and-aov.html): What conversion and average order value measure, the levers behind each, and where the store's sound environment fits among them.
- [Is Popular Music Always the Best Choice for Retail? (The Data Says No)](https://entuned.co/blog/is-popular-music-always-the-best-choice-for-retail-the-data-says-no.html): Popular music consistently underperforms in retail — and in some studies performs no better than silence.
- [Can the Wrong Music Actually REDUCE Your Sales?](https://entuned.co/blog/can-the-wrong-music-actually-reduce-your-sales.html): Yes — the wrong music actively reduces sales, not just fails to help.
- [Can Music Actually Distract Customers FROM Shopping?](https://entuned.co/blog/can-music-actually-distract-customers-from-shopping.html): Yes — music can hijack cognitive resources away from shopping decisions.
- [How Much Does a BMI Music License Cost? (And How to Avoid It)](https://entuned.co/blog/bmi-license-cost.html): BMI's published small-retail minimum is about $294 a year, but BMI is one of four PROs — the full licensing bill, and how to avoid needing it.
- [How to Choose a Music Service for Your Store](https://entuned.co/blog/best-retail-music-service.html): Seven things to evaluate before signing, how the major services compare on each, and why the biggest catalog usually isn't the right answer for a small store.
- [Why Do Some Stores Feel More Inviting Than Others?](https://entuned.co/blog/why-do-some-stores-feel-more-inviting-than-others.html): Whether a store feels inviting comes down to measurable sensory variables — and more stimuli can actually be worse.
- [How Does Music Shape Brand Perception?](https://entuned.co/blog/how-does-music-shape-brand-perception.html): Music doesn't just complement a brand — it becomes part of the brand identity in customers' minds.
- [Can Familiar Music Actually HURT Your Retail Sales?](https://entuned.co/blog/can-familiar-music-actually-hurt-your-retail-sales.html): Yes — familiar music makes customers leave faster.
- [What Is Dwell Time and Why Does It Matter?](https://entuned.co/blog/what-is-dwell-time-and-why-does-it-matter.html): Dwell time — total time a customer spends in your store — is one of the strongest predictors of unplanned purchases, but only when paired with the right emotional state.
- [How Does Tempo Affect Shoppers?](https://entuned.co/blog/how-does-tempo-affect-shoppers.html): Music tempo does not have a simple fast-or-slow effect on retail sales.
- [How Does Music Influence Emotions in Retail?](https://entuned.co/blog/how-does-music-influence-emotions-in-retail.html): Music is the fastest emotional lever in any retail environment — faster than lighting, scent, or visual merchandising.
- [How Does Music Affect Perceived Value?](https://entuned.co/blog/how-does-music-affect-perceived-value.html): Music reframes how customers perceive the value of products — the right soundtrack makes inventory feel worth more, while the wrong one makes it feel cheap.
- [How Does Music Affect Browsing Behavior?](https://entuned.co/blog/how-does-music-affect-browsing-behavior.html): Music affects what customers pick up, which direction they turn, and how many categories they explore — all without conscious awareness.
- [Does Slow Music Increase Sales?](https://entuned.co/blog/does-slow-music-increase-sales.html): Slow music does not reliably increase sales on its own.
- [Does Music Affect Willingness to Pay?](https://entuned.co/blog/does-music-affect-willingness-to-pay.html): Music can increase the maximum price a customer is willing to pay — but only for hedonic (pleasure-driven) products.
- [Does Fast Music Increase Sales?](https://entuned.co/blog/does-fast-music-increase-sales.html): Fast music can increase retail sales by approximately 8% — but only in crowded stores.
- [Why Music Is the Most Underrated Tool in Retail](https://entuned.co/blog/why-music-is-the-most-underrated-tool-in-retail.html): Music is the most underrated tool in retail because it operates across more psychological dimensions than any other environmental variable — tempo, volume, mode, genre, familiarity, and cultural assoc
- [The Science of Impulse Purchases (And How Music Triggers Them)](https://entuned.co/blog/the-science-of-impulse-purchases-and-how-music-triggers-them.html): Impulse purchases are driven by emotional state, not product displays — and the pleasure a customer feels in the first 5 minutes of entering a store is the strongest predictor of unplanned spending.
- [How Music Secretly Influences What You Buy (The Psychology of Purchasing)](https://entuned.co/blog/how-music-secretly-influences-what-you-buy-the-psychology-of-purchasin.html): Music influences purchasing decisions through four pathways: tempo drives variety-seeking behavior, cultural cues prime product selection, emotional state triggers impulse buys, and volume shifts cogn
- [Can Background Music Actually Increase Revenue? (140-Store Study Reveals the Truth)](https://entuned.co/blog/can-background-music-actually-increase-revenue-140-store-study-reveals.html): Yes — background music can increase revenue, but the effect is conditional.
- [What Music Should You Play in Your Store? (The Science-Backed Answer)](https://entuned.co/blog/what-music-should-you-play-in-your-store-the-science-backed-answer.html): The right store music isn't a genre — it's a system.
- [The Dwell Time Secret: How Music Keeps Customers in Your Store](https://entuned.co/blog/the-dwell-time-secret-how-music-keeps-customers-in-your-store.html): Music increases dwell time by up to 15 minutes per visit.
- [How Music Controls Customer Behavior (Without Them Knowing)](https://entuned.co/blog/how-music-controls-customer-behavior-without-them-knowing.html): Music controls customer behavior through at least four mechanisms: it changes walking speed (volume), dwell time (tempo), product selection (cultural priming), and impulse purchases (emotional state).
- [Can Music Make Customers Spend MORE? (What 43,000 Transactions Reveal)](https://entuned.co/blog/can-music-make-customers-spend-more-what-43000-transactions-reveal.html): Yes — music can increase customer spending by 8–15% depending on tempo, volume, genre, and context.
- [One Playlist for Everyone Is a Playlist for No One](https://entuned.co/blog/one-playlist-for-everyone-no-one.html): A mood filter is a menu, not a design tool. Every other element of a store works by specification. The music is the only thing still selected from a dropdown.
- [The Most Expensive Paperweight in Your Store](https://entuned.co/blog/most-expensive-paperweight-in-your-store.html): Forty years of research show music shapes dwell, conversion, and basket size. Most stores still use it as sonic furniture because nobody defined the job.
- [Madonna Never Got Your Design Brief](https://entuned.co/blog/madonna-never-got-your-design-brief.html): Every other layer of a retail store gets a written design brief. The music skips the process, and customers absorb whatever was already written for a different room.
- [You're Licensing Technology That Doesn't Work](https://entuned.co/blog/licensing-technology-that-doesnt-work.html): Retailers license software, fixtures, and music, but only the music was designed for a different room. The job was never defined, so the failure is invisible.
- [What If You Licensed Music the Way Film and TV Do?](https://entuned.co/blog/licensed-music-like-film-and-tv.html): Sync licensing gives film and TV music chosen for the scene, but the economics make it impossible for retail. Composition delivers the same intentional fit at retail rates.
- [Every Store Is About to Sound Different](https://entuned.co/blog/every-store-about-to-sound-different.html): Music is following scent design's trajectory into the brand experience layer. Early movers compound an outcome-data advantage that late adopters can't buy back.
- [The Most Expensive Air in Retail](https://entuned.co/blog/most-expensive-air-in-retail.html): Every variable in a retail store gets designed except the music. Six vignettes showing what borrowed catalog tracks are actually doing to a purchase in progress.
- [She Said Exactly What the Music Told Her to Say](https://entuned.co/blog/add-it-to-the-pile.html): A customer at the UNTUCKit pilot repeated an Entuned song lyric back as her buying decision without knowing it. Semantic priming through parameterized music.
- [The Invisible Obvious, Part 5: Sound](https://entuned.co/blog/invisible-obvious-05-sound.html): Music in retail is where lighting was in 1985. Forty years of research, no installed practice. The series payoff.
- [The Invisible Obvious, Part 4: Light](https://entuned.co/blog/invisible-obvious-04-light.html): The fifteen-year shift from "lighting is infrastructure" to "lighting design is a retail discipline with measurable ROI."
- [The Invisible Obvious, Part 3: Bodies](https://entuned.co/blog/invisible-obvious-03-bodies.html): How nonverbal communication moved from "soft" academic curiosity to a measurable variable taught in law school and MBA programs.
